"complementary" is described in-document as "distinct compatible information about a corresponding subject". I think blade pitch controller objective and pitch angle at a specific wind speed are complementary as properties for a wind turbine. But if the "subject" is different wind turbines, it doesn't fit the legend given. This may suggest that some more fine-grained categories are needed to judge comparisons, e.g. "these would be complementary if about the same subject, but they aren't or it's unclear whether they are". I know 'retrieval' doesn't have much semantic context; it's just a puny model doing its best! (We could try some alternative embedding models from DeepInfra, too.) But anyhow, this suggests the flaw is in part in our QA set, not providing the flexibility for counterfactuals like "would be" or "if only"
